title: NURS 1017 Unit 4 Case Study 4
description: 67-year-old male with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma receiving combination chemotherapy presenting with severe muscle wasting (cancer cachexia), painful oral mucositis, and acute febrile neutropenia requiring emergency oncologic nursing care.

question.stem: The nurse conducts an immediate emergency triage assessment on Gerald. Which clinical findings should the nurse recognize as critical cues indicating bone marrow suppression (febrile neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, severe anemia) and cancer cachexia? Select all that apply.

options.text: Severe temporal muscle wasting, sunken eyes, prominent ribs, and a 14% involuntary loss of body mass over 10 weeks despite nutritional supplements
Normal vigorous appetite with rapid 5 kg weight gain and generalized bilateral 3+ pitting pedal edema
Extensive oral erythema, ulcerations, and white pseudomembranous plaques causing excruciating pain on swallowing
Multiple scattered petechiae and ecchymoses on bilateral forearms with platelet count of 28 × 10⁹/L
Severe pallor, resting tachycardia (114 bpm), fatigue, and hemoglobin of 72 g/L
Oral temperature of 38.6 °C (101.5 °F) with absolute neutrophil count (ANC) of 320/mm³ (0.32 × 10⁹/L)

question.explanation: Gerald exhibits life-threatening complications of advanced cancer and cytotoxic chemotherapy: (Option 6) Febrile neutropenia (temp >= 38.3 °C with ANC < 500/mm³)—an oncologic emergency requiring immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics within 60 minutes due to absent inflammatory response; (Option 4) Severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 28 × 109/L) causing spontaneous cutaneous bleeding (petechiae, ecchymoses); (Option 5) Symptomatic severe anemia (hemoglobin 72 g/L with compensatory tachycardia and pallor); (Option 3) Grade 3 oral mucositis, serving as a painful barrier breakdown and prime portal for bacteremia/sepsis; and (Option 1) Cancer cachexia (profound wasting of skeletal muscle and adipose tissue driven by tumor-derived inflammatory cytokines). Rapid weight gain with pitting edema reflects volume overload/heart failure, not cachectic wasting.

rows.text: Profound skeletal muscle wasting, anorexia, and hypermetabolic state driven by tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) and interleukin-6 (IL-6)
Oral temperature of 38.6 °C with absolute neutrophil count of 320/mm³ creating extreme vulnerability to opportunistic bacterial sepsis
Multiple petechiae, spontaneous mucosal ecchymoses, and platelet count of 28 × 10⁹/L

question.preamble: Stat laboratory results have been returned from the hospital laboratory. The nurse has reviewed the Nurses' Notes from 1030 and the Laboratory Reports.
question.explanation:
1. Cancer Cachexia: A complex metabolic wasting syndrome mediated by tumor-derived and host-produced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-1, IL-6, interferon-gamma) causing accelerated proteolysis, lipolysis, and hypermetabolism that cannot be reversed by conventional nutritional intake.
2. Neutropenia / Leukopenia: Deficiency of circulating functional white blood cells / neutrophils (ANC < 500/mm³). Neutrophils form the primary cellular defense against bacteria and fungi; because neutrophils make up pus, severely neutropenic clients cannot mount a typical inflammatory purulent response, making fever often the sole sign of lethal infection.
3. Thrombocytopenia: Platelet count < 50 × 109/L dramatically impairs primary hemostatic plug formation, manifesting as petechiae, purpura, and increased bleeding risk.
4. Anemia: Reduced red blood cells (Hb 72 g/L) impairs tissue oxygenation, eliciting compensatory tachycardia and tachypnea.

question.stem:
The nurse synthesizes the client's clinical findings to establish immediate nursing priorities.

Complete the following sentences by choosing from the lists of options.
question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Nurses' Notes from 1100.
question.explanation:
1. Priority Threat: In febrile neutropenia (fever >= 38.3 °C with ANC < 500/mm³), microbial invasion (often endogenous flora translocating through broken mucosal barriers) can escalate to septic shock and death within hours. Administering broad-spectrum anti-pseudomonal beta-lactams within 60 minutes of arrival is an international emergency standard.
2. Lack of Pus / Fever as Solitary Sign: Neutrophils are required to create erythema, swelling, and pus. In their near-absence (ANC 320/mm³), local physical signs are muted, and fever is frequently the sole manifestation of bacteremia.
3. Cachexia vs. Starvation: In starvation, the body reduces basal metabolic rate and spares muscle protein while utilizing fat stores. In cancer cachexia, tumor cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6) drive profound hypercatabolism, proteolysis, and energy expenditure, causing refractory muscle and fat wasting that cannot be reversed by nutrition alone.

question.stem: The nurse plans comprehensive nursing interventions to manage Gerald's febrile neutropenia, bleeding risk, and oral mucositis. Which interventions should the nurse include in the plan of care? Select all that apply.

options.text: Encourage vigorous daily flossing and firm scrubbing of ulcerated oral mucosa to mechanically debride plaques
Implement bleeding precautions: avoid intramuscular injections, use soft-bristled toothbrushes or foam swabs, and avoid straight razors
Insert a rectal thermometer every 2 hours to closely track central core body temperature trends
Administer prescribed packed red blood cells to treat symptomatic severe anemia (hemoglobin 72 g/L)
Provide non-alcoholic, soothing oral rinses (e.g., sodium bicarbonate or salt-and-soda rinse) every 2 to 4 hours, avoiding commercial alcohol-based mouthwashes
Implement strict protective neutropenic precautions including private room placement, strict handwashing, and avoidance of fresh plants, flowers, or raw unpasteurized foods
Administer prescribed subcutaneous filgrastim (G-CSF) to accelerate granulocyte bone marrow production and recovery

question.preamble: The nurse has reviewed the Nurses' Notes from 1300 and the Clinical Care Protocol.
question.explanation: Appropriate nursing interventions include: (Option 6) Strict protective isolation to shield the immunocompromised client from opportunistic pathogens; (Option 2) Bleeding precautions (platelets 28 × 109/L) including avoiding IM injections, razor shaving, and hard toothbrushes; (Option 5) Gentle, alcohol-free oral hygiene (salt/soda rinses, topical analgesics) to treat mucositis without irritating raw mucosa; (Option 7) Administering G-CSF (filgrastim) to stimulate neutrophil production in the bone marrow; and (Option 4) Transfusing packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia with tachycardia. Rectal temperatures, suppositories, and enemas are strictly contraindicated in neutropenic and thrombocytopenic clients due to the risk of mucosal tearing, rectal abscess, and direct bacterial seeding into the bloodstream. Vigorous oral flossing causes mucosal laceration and bacteremia.

tabs.title: Clinical Care Protocol
tabs.content:
Neutropenic & Thrombocytopenic Safety Bundle:

  • Vital Signs: Check temperature q4h (oral or axillary only; NO RECTAL temps).
  • Environmental: No fresh flowers, plants, standing water; all visitors must mask and wash hands; low-microbial cooked diet only.
  • Bleeding Precautions: Apply pressure to venipunctures for minimum 5–10 minutes; soft foam oral swabs; electric razor only; fall precautions.
  • Medication: Filgrastim 300 mcg SC daily at 0900 until ANC > 1,500/mm³ × 2 consecutive days.

question.stem: The nurse is executing the daily clinical orders and monitoring Gerald on Day 2 of hospitalization. For each nursing action, click to specify whether the action is Indicated, Non-Essential, or Contraindicated.

rows.text: Inspect the oral mucosa, perianal region, skin folds, and vascular catheter exit site every shift for subtle erythema or tenderness
Administer prescribed oral nystatin swish-and-swallow suspension following oral hygiene to treat oral candidiasis
Administer aspirin or high-dose non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for breakthrough joint pain and fever reduction
Administer a stimulating rectal suppository or tap-water enema for mild constipation
Offer small, frequent, high-calorie, nutrient-dense soft foods at cool or room temperature
Obtain serial bilateral lower extremity radiographs every 12 hours

question.preamble: Day 2 inpatient oncology nursing monitoring. The nurse has reviewed the Nurses' Notes and Vital Signs from 0800 (Day 2).
question.explanation:
1. Indicated: Because neutropenic clients cannot produce pus, close physical inspection of potential breakdown sites (oral mucosa, catheter insertion site, perianal area) for subtle tenderness or erythema is vital.
2. Indicated: Nystatin treats opportunistic Candida albicans fungal superinfections common in immunocompromised clients with mucositis.
3. Contraindicated: Aspirin and NSAIDs inhibit platelet cyclooxygenase (worsening bleeding risk in severe thrombocytopenia) and can mask fevers.
4. Contraindicated: Rectal suppositories and enemas are strictly contraindicated due to risk of mucosal perforation, rectal hematoma, and systemic bacteremia.
5. Indicated: Soft, cool, non-acidic, high-protein foods minimize oral discomfort while providing caloric intake for cachexia.
6. Non-Essential: Repeated routine limb X-rays are clinically unjustified and expose the client to pointless radiation.

The nurse conducts discharge preparation and evaluates client and family understanding of home infection prevention and cachexia management.

question.preamble: Discharge evaluation on Day 4. The nurse has reviewed the Nurses' Notes from 1100 (Day 4).
question.explanation:
1. ANC Recovery: An ANC > 1,500/mm³ represents safe recovery of the neutrophil defense network, permitting discontinuation of protective isolation and resumption of outpatient status.
2. Febrile Threshold: In oncology, fever in a neutropenic client is defined as an oral temperature >= 38.3 °C (101.0 °F) once, or >= 38.0 °C (100.4 °F) sustained over 1 hour. This constitutes an immediate medical emergency requiring prompt blood cultures and broad-spectrum antibiotics.
3. Cachexia Nutritional Management: Since cytokines cause anorexia, early satiety, and hypercatabolism, small, calorie- and protein-dense meals served frequently throughout the day, supplemented with oral nutritional shakes and mild seasoning, provide the best nutritional maintenance without overwhelming the client.

First dose of IV piperacillin-tazobactam (4.5 g) infused within 45 minutes of arrival. Subcutaneous filgrastim (G-CSF) 300 mcg ordered daily to stimulate granulocyte production. Protective neutropenic precautions instituted (private room, meticulous hand hygiene, no fresh flowers/plants, no sick visitors, low-microbial cooked diet). Mucositis care protocol initiated.

1300:Gerald settled into private positive-pressure room on oncology unit. IV fluid bolus completed; blood pressure improved to 108/66 mmHg, HR 96 bpm. 1 unit of irradiated, leukoreduced packed red blood cells transfused via peripheral IV over 2 hours without reaction. Pre-medicated with nystatin oral suspension (swish and swallow) for oral candidiasis and compound lidocaine/diphenhydramine/antacid oral suspension for mucositis pain. Daughter instructed on protective precautions.

0800 (Day 2):Gerald is afebrile this morning (temp 37.0 °C). Blood pressure stable at 116/70 mmHg, HR 82 bpm. Morning blood counts: WBC 1.8 × 10⁹/L, ANC increased from 320 to 580/mm³. Hemoglobin improved to 88 g/L following transfusion. Platelets 32 × 10⁹/L; no new petechiae or mucosal bleeding. Client was able to swallow 120 mL of high-protein nutritional shake at room temperature with minimal pain after topical lidocaine rinse. IV piperacillin-tazobactam continues. Blood cultures from admission show no growth to date at 24 hours.

1100 (Day 4):Discharge education completed with Gerald and his daughter. Gerald is afebrile × 48 hours. ANC has recovered to 1,620/mm³, platelets 84 × 10⁹/L, hemoglobin 94 g/L. Oral mucositis has healed to Grade 1; client is eating soft scrambled eggs, cottage cheese, and high-protein puddings with minimal discomfort. Digital oral thermometer provided; daughter verbalizes emergency parameters (temp ≥ 38.0 °C for 1 hr or ≥ 38.3 °C once). Oncologist adjusted upcoming chemotherapy dosing by 20% to prevent severe marrow suppression. Home health nurse scheduled to visit tomorrow.

tabs.title: Clinical Care Protocol
tabs.content:
Neutropenic & Thrombocytopenic Safety Bundle:

  • Vital Signs: Check temperature q4h (oral or axillary only; NO RECTAL temps).
  • Environmental: No fresh flowers, plants, standing water; all visitors must mask and wash hands; low-microbial cooked diet only.
  • Bleeding Precautions: Apply pressure to venipunctures for minimum 5–10 minutes; soft foam oral swabs; electric razor only; fall precautions.
  • Medication: Filgrastim 300 mcg SC daily at 0900 until ANC > 1,500/mm³ × 2 consecutive days.
